acceptance_proposals.visual: Leading forelimb extends forward/down while opposite forelimb folds and a hindlimb drives rearward; recognisable in side and quarter views.
Reach leads into forepaw landing followed by fore support/push; body pitch/height follows support and hind legs begin gathering without a whole-body sudden drop.

Carpus folds under chest and both hind legs/paws gather forward under abdomen, clearly narrower than extended silhouette. Core flex participates instead of keeping a long straight torso and widening feet about fixed neutral centres.
Hind landing/load precedes next fore reach; sequential timing is readable through one complete cycle and repeats in the same order.

Hip/chest/head height and lumbar curve pass through compression/recovery without the previous84.6mm global IK dip or rebound pop. Neck/head lean forward/down with nose near the back line; hip-top skin remains rounded and connected during extension.
acceptance_proposals.numerical: Inspect actual evaluated hip/chest/head velocities and discrete acceleration at120Hz, key boundaries and seam. Source/design C2 curves do not substitute for final evaluated pose measurements.

acceptance_proposals.visual: Elbow/carpus/stifle/hock/toe motion remains connected and correctly bent; toe pitch progresses through landing, drive and recovery without a short abrupt switch or foot collapse.
acceptance_proposals.numerical: Evaluate actual skinned foot region ankle+toe influence≥.65 including heel, sampled foot/ankle rotations and sagittal bend signs. Whole-body floor margin unchanged from previous validation.

acceptance_proposals.visual: Supported soles remain plausible on the moving ground, airborne phases remain visible, and the repeated boundary is smooth in normal and half-speed decoded frame progression.
acceptance_proposals.numerical: At declared nominal speed compute actual fixed sole skin drift for each supported phase, whole-body skin floor, four-paw clearance and loop kinematics. Numerical stability and visual rhythm judged separately; no absolute zero-skating claim.
